title: The Gold Journey
subtitle: A live trade journal: Prof Tan's gold position and Claude's calls, scored against what actually happened
position: Buy 4,124 (Thu 22 Oct ~03:00 SGT) and buy 4,102 (Thu 22 Oct ~13:00 SGT)
2 GC (average ≈ 4,107.5, implied by open P/L) + 1 MGC (average ≈ 4,280, implied; carried from earlier)
levels: 4,015–4,020 (Fri night cap), then 4,037–4,050, then 4,068–4,076 (broken summer base)
3,989–4,005 (Fri post-data low). Below 3,989: no support on the 6-month chart

events.title: Missed move that started it all
events.call: Gold rallied about 30 points off the 09:00 SGT Asian open (4,134.5 → 4,166.4 by 11:00) and Prof missed it.
events.outcome: Question raised: is 09:00 SGT a special time for gold?

events.title: How big will the 09:00 hour be?
events.call: Claude, from 21 sessions of hourly bars: the 09:00 SGT hour typically moves about 20 points (median 19.8), roughly 1.5× a normal hour.

events.title: Which way at 09:00?
events.call: Claude: gold is in a downtrend, so if 4,130 breaks it should run to 4,110, then 4,095.
events.outcome: 4,130 broke to 4,124.0 and immediately reversed to 4,142.7. A stop run, not a breakdown.
events.lesson: The trend argument was over-weighted; the fakeout behaviour had not been tested yet.

events.title: The alternative scenario
events.call: Claude: if 4,130 holds, expect a bounce into the 4,145–4,150 sellers and short there.
events.outcome: Bounce peaked at 4,142.7, about 2 points short of the zone, then faded.

events.title: Research: the 09:00 pre-open break
events.call: Claude measured the 09:00 hour against the 06:00–09:00 range: it took out one side in 20 of 21 sessions. 22 Sept–9 Oct most breaks held (8 of 10); 12–21 Oct every one-sided break failed (6 of 6). The live dashboard was rebuilt to flag failed breaks at 09:00.
events.outcome: A useful lead, small sample. See 22 Oct for how it ended.

events.title: Will the 4,124 buy fill?
events.call: Prof placed a buy limit at 4,124, that morning's exact low. Claude: roughly 50–55% tonight (62% historical base rate, trimmed for a light-data night). Warned that an order at the exact low may not fill, and that a flush through it catches the stop run.
events.outcome: At about 03:00 SGT gold flushed to 4,122.4 on heavy volume and filled the order, then V-reversed to 4,164.9 by 06:00.

events.title: How volatile tonight?
events.call: Claude: a light-data night, so expect a smaller-than-average move unless oil jumps.
events.outcome: A 37-point flush at 02:30 SGT (14:30 New York) and a full recovery.
events.lesson: 02:00–03:00 SGT is usually quiet; thin post-settlement liquidity makes stop runs possible.

events.title: Long from 4,124: where is the stop?
events.call: Claude: put a structural stop near 4,127 before 09:00. Do not put a tight stop just under 4,147, because the 09:00 sweep would take it out.
events.outcome: No stop was placed.

events.title: The drift: protect the gain
events.call: Claude, with the trade +18.5: either bank it now and re-buy a failed break at 09:00, or hold with the 4,127 stop.
events.outcome: Prof held without a stop; an exit near 4,150 wasn't done in time.

events.title: Saudi Aramco strike
events.call: A drone strike on a Saudi Aramco oil field killed two people; the U.S. ordered non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia (Investing.com, 00:52 GMT).
events.outcome: Oil higher, rate-hike fears higher, gold lower.

events.title: The 09:00 rule meets real news
events.call: 09:00 swept the pre-open low to 4,123.7 and closed back inside: the dashboard's 'failed break down, fade long' signal.
events.outcome: At 11:15 SGT 4,122 broke on the day's heaviest volume and the signal failed. The 6-of-6 run ended.

events.title: Where to double up?
events.call: Claude (with the IBKR feed down): add only at 4,122–4,124 after a sweep-and-reclaim; don't add if a 5-minute bar closes below 4,119.
events.outcome: The break below 4,122 had already happened at 11:15. The answer was built on stale levels.
events.lesson: Don't advise on levels without live data; say so and wait.

events.title: Averaging down at 4,102
events.call: Prof's second buy at 4,102, just under the 4,103.3 base. Claude: good placement to catch a sweep, but a headline turns it into a breakdown; breakeven would be ~4,113, right at the first sellers.
events.outcome: It filled, and gold broke the month low (4,091) to 4,082.3 by 14:00.

events.title: Units: MGC or GC?
events.call: Claude priced the risk at $10 a point (MGC). Prof pointed out it was $100 a point. The position was 2 GC + 1 MGC: $210 per point.
events.outcome: Every dollar figure for the GC had been 10× too small.
events.lesson: Confirm the contract and multiplier before quoting dollars.

events.title: Cut one GC into the bounce
events.call: Gold bounced 24 points to 4,106. Claude: sell one GC into 4,103–4,105 to halve the risk. A second chance came at 20:30–21:00 SGT (4,107.2).
events.outcome: Not taken.

events.title: 'Stocks down + yields down = gold up'
events.call: Claude's rule for the safe-haven thesis: when stocks fall and yields fall, gold should catch a bid.
events.outcome: Thursday delivered exactly that: the 10-year fell 17 bp to 4.972% (biggest drop since March 2023) and the Nasdaq fell ~2.4%. Gold fell ~110 points anyway.
events.lesson: With yields near 5%, Treasuries took the haven role; gold pays nothing.

events.title: Reading the jobless claims
events.call: Claude inferred from gold's first two minutes that the number 'wasn't strong'.
events.outcome: Claims were 194K vs 200K expected: stronger, i.e. hawkish.
events.lesson: Read the number, not the first tick.

events.title: Summer base breaks
events.call: At the New York open gold broke the 4,070–4,076 June–July base and slid all night toward 4,037.
events.outcome: A 4,068 stop would have exited here.

events.title: Sellers at 4,046–4,053
events.call: Claude, with gold at 4,032: the nearest sellers are 4,046–4,053; cut one GC into a bounce there; hard stop ~4,008 under the 6-month low.
events.outcome: 08:55 bounce peaked at 4,047.5 inside the zone and was rejected; 09:00 fell 13 points in 4 minutes.

events.title: Sweep and reclaim of the floor
events.call: Claude described two outcomes for the 4,015 floor: a sweep-and-reclaim, or a breakdown.
events.outcome: Gold swept to 4,000.9, then snapped back above 4,030. (A 4,008 stop would have filled near the low.)

events.title: Loss aversion
events.call: Prof: hold until breakeven. Claude: breakeven needs ~76 points through three seller zones; keep one GC for the recovery, sell the other on strength, hard stop under 4,000.

events.title: What will move gold Friday night?
events.call: Claude: the 22:00 SGT inflation-expectations data matter most; a rise is bad for gold.
events.outcome: Inflation expectations rose to 4.7% (1-yr) and 3.5% (5-yr), the highest since May; PMI output prices hit 59.8, highest since Aug 2022. Gold fell from 4,037 to 3,989 in 30 minutes on the week's heaviest volume.

events.title: Week closes
events.call: Gold closes the week at 4,009.5. Position held into the weekend (to confirm).
events.outcome: Next: Monday 06:00 SGT reopen with weekend headline risk.

lessons: The clock was reliable, direction was not. Calls about when gold moves (09:00 and 20:00–23:00 SGT) held up; calls about which way it would go were close to a coin flip.
Every stop level discussed was later reached (4,127, then 4,068, then 4,008). Placing a stop is a decision made in calm; not placing one is a decision made under pressure.
Averaging down into a news-driven break doubled the exposure just as the regime changed.
Know the multiplier before quoting dollars: GC is $100 per point, MGC $10.
In this regime Treasuries, not gold, are the safe haven. Gold fell on the one setup that normally lifts it.
No advice on levels without a live feed. When data drops, say so and wait.
next: Monday 06:00 SGT reopen: weekend Saudi/Iran headlines can gap gold either way.

Expiry: the December contract enters its delivery period at the end of November. Long holders usually need to exit or roll before first notice day (around 30 Nov, to be confirmed in TOS), and brokers often close positions a few days earlier. So the runway is about five weeks, not until December.
This page will be updated as the position develops, until it is closed.
